title: Ang 557: Vadhans begins
hookLine: Guru Nanak opens the raga of weddings and mourning
tomorrow: so how did heritage night go, and who ended up side by side?

lines: CAN A LOVER OF GOD DISLIKE ANYONE?
cards: Watch what happens in a stadium when the home team scores. Strangers hug strangers. Nobody checks anyone's job or neighborhood.
Love for one thing spills over onto everyone near it. Vadhans, a raga tradition links with weddings and with mourning, opens on ang 557 with Guru Nanak describing that same spill.
And it answers the question straight: can someone in love with God dislike anyone? Not by this line.

teach.h: THE ADDICT, THE FISH, THE LOVER.
teach.b: So, one question: what does loving God do to how you see people? Guru Nanak, in paraphrase: the addict can't do without his drug, and the fish can't do without water.

teach.h: DYED IN LOVE, EVERYONE IS DEAR.
teach.b: And those dyed in love for their Lord find everyone dear. It's a bold picture, right after yesterday's two cups. The same pull an addict feels, turned toward the One, and what it produces is warmth toward everybody.
Elsewhere the Gurus say why: the One's light is in everyone. A neighbor tradition ties these two loves together too, in its own words.

teach.h: A NEIGHBOR: LOVE THE ONE YOU SEE.
teach.b: In the New Testament, the First Letter of John says: "If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?"
That's the shared thing, and it's real. Two scriptures saying love for God shows up as love for the people in front of you. And here's the honest difference.

John writes to fellow Christians, and just before this he says we love because God first loved us, a love he sees made known in Jesus. Guru Nanak speaks of a soul dyed in her Lord's love, and of one light in all.
Different roads to the same table, and neither has to become the other.

how: Sikhs reading the Granth in order reach Vadhans after Bihagra; tradition links the raga with weddings and with mourning, and its hymns are sung in kirtan.

o: where Guru Nanak's raga Asa begins

games.q: the spill of love — tap the pairs.
p: love the brother you have seen

s: Vadhans opens with an addict and a fish
the addict can't do without his drug, the fish without water; so it is with those dyed in the Lord's love.
the line means lovers of God should love only other believers
those dyed in their Lord's love find everyone dear.
Guru Nanak's line and 1 John 4:20 say exactly the same thing
both tie love of God to love of people; John writes to Christians of a love made known in Jesus, the Guru of a soul dyed in her Lord's love and one light in all.

games.q: at your cousin's wedding, two uncles who haven't spoken in years end up at the same table. one asks you to move his seat. by ang 557, what fits?
o: keep the seats and bring them both a plate; love for the One makes room for both.
move him; loving God means keeping the peace by keeping people apart.
tell them both to apologize first, and then they can share the table.
games.why: those dyed in their Lord's love find everyone dear. the line doesn't sort people first and love them after.

practice: Close your eyes and bring to mind one face you find hard: not the hardest, just a hard one. Hold it gently for the sit without fixing anything, and let the line rest beside it: dyed in love, everyone is dear.
If you'd like, read the opening of ang 557 first.

wordCard.voice: Ang 557. Where Vadhans begins, with Guru Nanak's addict, his fish, and a lover of God who finds everyone dear.
